clinicalPearls: The most common form of axonal CMT (CMT2), caused predominantly by autosomal dominant mutations in MFN2, which encodes mitofusin 2.
The neuropathy is axonal: conduction velocities are normal or near-normal while motor and sensory amplitudes are reduced, distinguishing it from the demyelinating CMT1 group.
Onset is frequently early and the course comparatively severe, with a notable proportion losing independent ambulation, though milder later-onset cases occur.
Optic atrophy may accompany the neuropathy (a phenotype historically labelled HMSN VI), and some patients show central nervous system or white-matter involvement.
Mitofusin 2 mediates mitochondrial fusion and axonal mitochondrial transport, explaining the vulnerability of the longest fibres.
Presents with length-dependent distal weakness, wasting and sensory loss, pes cavus and areflexia.
Diagnosis is by MFN2 sequencing, usually as part of an axonal-neuropathy gene panel.
reference.pathophysiology: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2A is caused, in most cases, by autosomal dominant mutations in MFN2, which encodes mitofusin 2, a GTPase of the outer mitochondrial membrane that mediates mitochondrial fusion and regulates the transport and distribution of mitochondria along axons. Impaired fusion and trafficking deprive the distal reaches of the longest axons of adequate mitochondrial function, producing a length-dependent axonal rather than demyelinating neuropathy, so conduction velocities are relatively preserved while motor and sensory amplitudes fall. The metabolic vulnerability of long fibre tracts also accounts for the associated optic atrophy and occasional central nervous system involvement seen in some patients. Onset is frequently early with a comparatively severe course, although later-onset milder presentations occur, and rare recessive and de novo cases are recognised.
additionalDifferentials: Other CMT2 subtypes (for example late-onset MPZ, RAB7, GARS, HSPB1 disease)
CMT1 subtypes, if any conduction slowing is present
Acquired axonal neuropathies (toxic, metabolic or nutritional)
Mitochondrial disease presenting with peripheral neuropathy
additionalInvestigations: Nerve conduction studies confirming an axonal pattern (low amplitudes, preserved velocities)
Ophthalmological assessment including optic nerve evaluation and visual evoked potentials
MRI brain where central features are suspected
Needle electromyography for chronic denervation and reinnervation
Family segregation studies and genetic counselling
redFlags: Very early onset with rapid progression and loss of ambulation
Central signs such as spasticity or white-matter change
reference.prognosis: The disease is often more severe than other forms of CMT2; early-onset cases may lose independent ambulation during childhood or adolescence, whereas later-onset disease follows a milder course.
pitfalls: Expecting demyelinating slowing, when CMT2A is axonal with near-normal velocities.
Missing optic atrophy as an integral part of the syndrome.
Overlooking rare recessive or de novo inheritance when a clear dominant pedigree is absent.
Attributing an axonal neuropathy to acquired causes without considering a genetic aetiology.
management: Provide supportive management with physiotherapy and occupational therapy, since no disease-modifying drug therapy exists
Fit ankle-foot orthoses and provide podiatry, footwear and walking aids for foot drop and pes cavus, with wheelchair provision where ambulation is lost
Offer orthopaedic foot surgery for disabling fixed deformity
Treat neuropathic pain symptomatically and avoid neurotoxic drugs such as vincristine
Screen for optic atrophy with ophthalmological assessment and visual evoked potentials, and evaluate for central nervous system involvement where features suggest it
Provide intensive rehabilitation for the frequently severe early-onset cases that lose independent ambulation
Offer genetic counselling for autosomal dominant inheritance and assess at-risk relatives
Coordinate multidisciplinary neuromuscular, ophthalmology, orthopaedic and rehabilitation care
